newsitem.title: USA: EU official sees tough issues in meat talks.
newsitem.headline: EU official sees tough issues in meat talks.

text.p: The senior European Union negotiator at bilateral talks on meat import inspection regulations predicted Tuesday "tough discussions" ahead for U.S. and EU officials in the next few days as they make a last-ditch effort to ward off a trade war.

"We've got a couple of days ahead of us with some tough discussions and we'll hope that by the end we'll have some kind of an agreement," EU's Lars Hoelgaard told reporters on his way into talks with U.S. Agriculture Department officials, including senior USDA trade official Paul Drazek.
EU officials arrived back in Washington late Monday to resume so-called veterinary equivalency discussions which ended last week without agreement by an April 1 deadline.
Negotiators lunched together Tuesday, and officially began talks in midafternoon. Discussions were expected to last well into the evening.

Both sides have imposed new meat and poultry inspection regulations that could stop some $50 million worth of U.S. poultry products going to Europe and halt $300 million worth of European meat products, mostly Danish and Italian hams, from being shipped to the United States.
Hoelgaard said the main sticking points were U.S. poultry processing procedures and the use of decontamination.
He said he was scheduled to go back to Brussels on Thursday evening "and by then we should know where we are." Hoelgaard said the EU side was hoping to narrow down the remaining differences.
U.S. poultry producers said they were unwilling to back away from improvements in food safety standards in order to meet the demands of the EU.
